title: GO Command Center Liveness Request Transport V1
description: One relay report: what the transport did with the newest fresh liveness probe, on one branch, with the boundedness facts restated on every run. A report is a record of a git push, never an authorisation: this component holds no Task key, signs nothing, and has no way to create, merge or close a pull request.

result.description: PUBLISHED moved the transport. ALREADY_PUBLISHED means this bucket is already on the bus, which is what makes a five-minute timer idempotent against a thirty-minute probe interval. SKIPPED_STALE declined to publish a probe the Bridge would have refused. REFUSED is fail-closed: nothing was pushed.

transport_branches.description: How many branches this transport will ever occupy. The pull request follows the branch, so the open-PR count cannot grow with the probe rate.

requests_per_submission.description: The Bridge accepts a submission only when the diff against the merge base with main is exactly one added requests/*.json, so a cycle adds one file and removes none.

api_client.description: No HTTP client in the tool at all, asserted against its own source by run_checks. The tool speaks git over SSH with the key the bus already trusts.

archive_is_append_only.description: A superseded probe is moved to request/liveness-archive before the transport drops it, and a path the archive already holds is never rewritten. Without the archive the projection would emit one REQUEST_FACT_WITHOUT_REQUEST anomaly per probe, because a Request fact is immutable while the file would be gone.

added_vs_main.description: Every path this submission adds to main. Exactly one, by assertion: the relay refuses rather than pushes when it is not.

removed_vs_main.description: Every path this submission removes from main. Always empty: a deletion would be a second diff entry and the Bridge would ignore the submission.

x-go-transport-rules.one_branch_one_pr: The transport is one long-lived branch. The operator opens its pull request once; every cycle force-updates the branch and the pull request follows. A new head is a new submission identity to the Bridge, so a reused branch is still a fresh submission.
x-go-transport-rules.why_not_accumulate: Accumulating request files on the transport branch would make every submission show more than one change, and the Bridge ignores a submission whose diff is not exactly one added request file.
x-go-transport-rules.why_an_archive: Facts are immutable and permanent and the projection attributes each one to the Request file it was read from, so a superseded file has to stay on the bus. request/* is the second namespace the state contract already declares for Requests; the projector collects it and the Bridge does not read it.
x-go-transport-rules.never_a_general_publisher: The outbox Request must be exactly the five common fields, in HK-STAGING-01, with CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH. This tool has no code path that publishes any other action, and holds no Task key.

x-go-non-authority: A relay report is a record of a git push. It authorises nothing and grants no execution.
The tool signs nothing, holds no private key and has no code path to the Bridge, the agent or an executor.
It cannot create, merge, close or revert a pull request: it holds no HTTP client and pushes branches only.
